simple_description: A recurrent throbbing headache that usually affects one side of the head, worsens with movement, and is often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light and sound.
medical_description: A neurovascular headache disorder characterized by recurrent attacks lasting 4 to 72 hours, typically unilateral, pulsating, of moderate to severe intensity, aggravated by routine physical activity, and associated with nausea, vomiting, photophobia, and phonophobia, without preceding aura symptoms.
affected_system: Trigeminovascular system, cranial blood vessels, and brainstem pain-modulating pathways.
symptoms: Moderate to severe throbbing or pulsating head pain
Pain typically on one side of the head (unilateral), though can be bilateral
Worsening of pain with physical exertion (walking, climbing stairs)
Fatigue, neck stiffness, and irritability during attack
early_warning_signs: Prodrome 24-48 hours before pain: frequent yawning, food cravings, mood swings, neck stiffness, fluid retention
possible_causes: Activation of the trigeminovascular system causing neurogenic inflammation and arterial vasodilation
Release of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) and substance P
risk_factors: Female sex (3 times higher in females after puberty)
High psychological stress, sleep deprivation, or skipping meals
Certain sensory triggers (flickering lights, strong perfumes, weather changes)
disease_types: Episodic migraine without aura (< 15 headache days per month)
clinical_evaluation: Diagnosed clinically based on ICHD-3 criteria (at least 5 attacks lasting 4-72 hours with characteristic features). Neurological physical examination is normal.
diagnostic_tests: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (3T Brain MRI) - Recommended only if 'red flags' (SNOOP criteria) or abnormal focal neurological examination are present to exclude secondary pathology
Non-contrast Head CT - If acute sudden onset to rule out intracranial hemorrhage
treatment_overview: Stratified acute therapy based on attack severity. Mild to moderate attacks treated with NSAIDs; moderate to severe attacks with 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonists (triptans) or oral CGRP receptor antagonists (gepants). Preventive therapy if >= 4 headache days/month.
medication_classes: Preventive classes: Beta-blockers (Propranolol), Antiepileptics (Topiramate), CGRP monoclonal antibodies
precautions: Avoid overusing acute pain medications (> 10 days/month for triptans) to prevent medication-overuse headache
Maintain consistent sleep schedule and regular hydration
Do not consume known food triggers (aged cheeses, MSG, nitrates, excess caffeine)
prevention: Maintain a migraine diary tracking triggers and timing
Practice stress-reduction techniques (mindfulness, progressive muscle relaxation)
Stay well-hydrated and avoid skipping meals
complications: Status migrainosus (debilitating migraine attack lasting > 72 hours)
emergency_signs: Sudden explosive thunderclap headache reaching maximum intensity in < 1 minute
Accompanying high fever, stiff neck, confusion, or rash
New neurological deficit: unilateral weakness, numbness, facial droop, or speech loss

faqs.question: Is migraine just a severe headache?
faqs.answer: No. Migraine is a complex neurological disorder involving nerve signaling, blood vessel reactivity, and brain chemical releases like CGRP, accompanied by systemic symptoms like nausea and sensory hypersensitivity.

faqs.question: When should medication be taken?
faqs.answer: Acute abortive medications (such as triptans or NSAIDs) are most effective when taken right at the onset of the mild headache phase, rather than waiting for the pain to become severe.

hi.name: माइग्रेन बिना ऑरा (Migraine without aura)
hi.summary: सिर के एक हिस्से में धड़कने वाला तेज़ दर्द जो 4 से 72 घंटे तक रहता है, साथ ही उल्टी, रोशनी और आवाज़ से परेशानी होती है।
hi.advice: अंधेरे शांत कमरे में आराम करें, माथे पर ठंडी पट्टी रखें और डॉक्टर द्वारा बताई गई माइग्रेन रोधी दवा लें।

hinglish.advice: Andhere kamre me rest karein, cold pack lagayein aur dehydration se bachein.
